cases.message: Retries happen when the worker times out, and sometimes two workers pick up the same job; I want to be sure we never charge twice.

Here is my design after three hours with the whiteboard: the shop service owns orders, stock counts, prices and coupons; the courier adapter owns labels and tracking; the mailer owns every message to a customer and nothing else sends one. No service reads another's tables; each is asked through its own interface. Orders and stock have one writer each. A refund starts in the shop service, is approved in the mailer's queue and appears in the dashboard as a pinned copy of the order.
The member's tier and the coupon type decide the discount; gold plus stacked coupons can never exceed 40%. Check every combination.

cases.message: Here is how I want the billing retries to work, after a morning with the incident notes. A charge request goes to the provider with an idempotency key made from the invoice id and the attempt window, not the attempt number, so two workers that pick up the same job send the same key. A worker that times out must not retry on its own; it marks the job as uncertain and the reconciler asks the provider for the state of that key before anything else happens. Refunds follow the same rule. I also want the reconciler to be the only writer of the final state, and the dashboards to read from it, never from the workers. If any of this conflicts with the current schema, tell me where before you change it. I care most that a customer is never charged twice, even when the provider is slow and the queue redelivers.

recent.text: We had another double charge on Tuesday. Can you look at the retry path?
I found two places where a worker retries after a timeout: the charge worker and the refund worker. Both build the idempotency key from the attempt number.
Don't change anything yet. I want to write down how it should work first.
